One month. A better welcome.

A better welcome, one scan away

The aim is to learn which short-term rental hosts recognise the problem, earn useful conversations and make the product easy to understand before launch. Keep the current Facebook-first approach. No new prices, launch promises or sign-up links in this month's copy.

Starts after the existing seven-post launch week, which is preserved below. These are 30 new daily content cards: 17 main posts and 13 Story-only days. Strategy & audience

The job of the month

Primary audience: Australian short-term rental hosts and owner-managers with one or a few holiday properties, especially those already answering guest questions or leaving a paper guide or guestbook. This is the working audience, to test through conversations—not a validated market-size claim.

Positioning: one QR display opens your welcome, house guidance, local favourites and a guest memory wall. Guests use their phone's browser without creating an account. The product is for a stay; it is not a tool for collecting booking-platform ratings.

Four messages to test

  1. Arrival: let guests find the next useful answer.
  2. Local knowledge: make the welcome feel personal.
  3. Memories: invite a note or photo without a guest sign-up.
  4. Host control: explain preview, approval and moderation accurately.

Boundaries for the copy

  • Prelaunch CTA: follow the Page or answer one useful question. Launch availability is announced only when ready.
  • Use genuine product screens and the real logo. Label the made-up demo property and sample messages. No invented customers, testimonials or poll results.
  • No promises of fewer messages, more bookings, better ratings, higher income or perfect automated screening.
  • No paid ads in this month. Proposed cash budget: A$0, using existing assets. Reserve roughly 3–4 hours a week for production, review and responding, then adjust to actual effort.
  • Keep private credentials, real guest data and private in-stay links out of public artwork.

Campaign, weekly rhythm & production

A better welcome, one scan away

Dates: 23 October–21 November 2026. Four full weeks plus two closing days. There is no discount, promo code or artificial deadline.

WeekFocusLearning question
1Make the arrival easierWhich arrival questions do hosts recognise?
2Put local knowledge to workWhat local tips feel useful?
3Give the property a memoryWhich memory prompt gets a response?
4Show the host's sideWhat prevents a host trying the product?
5Listen, then choose the next monthWhat should the next walkthrough answer?

One weekly production block

  1. Read genuine host replies and the last scorecard. Keep names and private messages out of artwork.
  2. Prepare the week's two feed graphics, carousel slides, reel and Story cards from the briefs. Use existing real demo captures or record current product screens.
  3. Review captions, demo labels, legibility, alt text and every visible product claim.
  4. After the owner's review, create native drafts where supported. Schedule only the approved final assets and confirm their times in Meta.
  5. Spend a short daily block responding to comments. Keep a weekly record of the questions, not invented quotes.

Five reels have shot-by-shot scripts; four carousels have slide outlines. A reference image or script is not an exported video or finished carousel. New content starts at Planned for that reason.

Needs you · decisions and checks

Before anything new goes out

  1. Review the 30 captions and visual briefs here. Approve, request changes or skip each item.
  2. Check the existing 19–22 October items in Business Suite before adding new drafts. Their recorded statuses below were imported from the earlier plan, not reverified today.
  3. Confirm the public website destination before changing the follow-only CTA to a demo or sign-up link. The current plan intentionally makes no public-domain or launch-date promise.
  4. Complete the launch checks and resolve the recorded testing issues before announcing general availability. The NAS testing checklist is the place to record proof.
  5. Decide on Instagram separately if you want it. This month works as a Facebook-only plan.
Weekly scorecard & next-month decision

What would make the month useful?

Working learning targets, not forecasts: collect at least ten substantive host replies and hold five willing-host conversations across the month. Establish the actual starting follower and reach numbers before interpreting growth. Do not report zero where a metric is unavailable.

MeasureRecordDecision it supports
FollowersStart/end from Page InsightsIs the intended audience starting to gather?
Reach and engagementPer post and format; record denominatorsWhich topics merit another attempt?
Substantive host repliesCount actual hosting questions or experience, not emoji-only repliesDoes the problem resonate?
Reel watch dataAvailable watch/completion measures in MetaDo people reach the explanation?
Production effortMinutes spent by formatCan the cadence be maintained?
Willing-host conversationsCount and anonymised themes; quote only with permissionWhat still needs explaining or changing?

Review dates

29 October, 5 November, 12 November and 19 November; final review 21 November. Compare formats cautiously if their reach is small or different. Keep the strongest useful topic, rewrite the weak explanation and choose the next month's cadence from evidence. No paid-ad spend is triggered automatically.

Conversation prompts: How do guests find your house information now? What do they ask again? Where does the current approach work well? What would stop you using a digital guestbook? What would you need to see in a demo?

Files, sources & how to edit

The NAS is the shared master

\\192.168.1.71\nas\projects\DigiStayBook\marketing\MARKETING_PLAN.html

  • Month content source — captions, Stories, format, visual briefs, alt text and shot/slide outlines.
  • build_marketing_plan.py + marketing-review.js + _reference/plan.css — rebuild this page locally with Python; no network or publishing action.
  • Reference-screen provenance — copies and hashes of the existing launch-pack demo screens. No new stock or AI-generated imagery.
  • DigiGuestbook marketing hub — reference for layout and review workflow; its event offers, prices and posting activity are not copied into DigiStayBook.
  • DigiStayBook operating plan and the existing prelaunch content source — product positioning and current prelaunch constraints.
  • Editing instructions — source edits, rebuilding and saving a portable review.

Browser edits are not automatically shared across computers. Download a review JSON or copy the review text, then consolidate approved changes into the source. The page contacts no external service.
